adjudicated_statement: Let H and X be algebraic stacks. Suppose a subset S of the geometric points |X| is defined as the image of a classifying morphism attached functorially, in the 2-Yoneda sense, to smooth surjective finite-type atlases of H: for every such atlas V->H from an algebraic space there is a finite-type morphism f_V:Z_V->X, and these morphisms are compatible with pullback along morphisms of atlases. Then for any two such atlases V->H and V'->H, the 2-fibre product W=V x_H V' exists as an algebraic space (Stacks Project Tag 04T2); the projections W->V and W->V' are smooth and surjective, hence surjective on geometric points (Tags 04XH, 04XI); and W->H is again a smooth surjective atlas. If Z_(-) is constructed only for scheme bases, one must pass to a scheme presentation of W. The tautological family on Z_W is then the pullback of the families on Z_V and Z_{V'}, so the geometric images of f_V, f_{V'}, and f_W in |X| coincide. Consequently S is independent of the atlas, and the unique reduced closed substack Y of X with |Y| equal to the Zariski closure of S (Tag 0509) is independent of the atlas. Common refinement of atlases of H does not by itself produce a morphism [H/G]->X or identify S with the image arising from an atlas of the quotient: a morphism [H/G]->X exists if and only if the classifying morphism from H is G-equivariant, equivalently the X-valued moduli point is G-invariant on geometric points (Tag 04WM). This lemma does not assert that a scheme-level tautological model constructed on atlases of H transfers to etale atlases of [H/G], and it does not assert atlas-independence of compactly supported cohomology of the atlas. In the campaign case (g,n)=(6,6), with H=H^bal the balanced tetragonal stack, X=M_{6,6}, and G=PGL_2, the extra invariance is ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7; the failure of ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 to transfer to atlases of Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2] is the separate finding FND-0187.
contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. Local originating artifacts were inspected first. ATT-0120 Section 3 and CLM-0120-2/6 argue that if V->H^bal and V'->H^bal are smooth finite-type atlases then W=V x_{H^bal} V' is a smooth atlas, tautological families on Z_W pull back from both sides, geometric images in |M_{6,6}| coincide, and the reduced closure Y is atlas-independent; passage to [H^bal/PGL_2] is separated off as PGL_2-invariance of the M_{6,6}-valued point via CLM-0112-7. REV-0170 confirmed those claims and extracted the present candidate. The stack-theoretic core is independently supplied by the Stacks Project: 2-fibre products of algebraic stacks exist (Tag 04T2/04TD); if V and V' are schemes then W is an algebraic space, not necessarily a scheme (Tag 04TF); |W|->|V| x_{|H|}|V'| is surjective (Tag 04XH) and a representable smooth surjection is surjective on geometric points (Tag 04XI); the topology on |H| is independent of the smooth atlas precisely by the same common-refinement square U''=U x_H U' (Tags 04XL/04XE); and a closed subset of |X| underlies a unique reduced closed substack (Tag 0509). Quotient morphisms [H/G]->X correspond to G-equivariant data (Tag 04WM/04UV), so G-invariance is an extra hypothesis, not a consequence of refining atlases of H. Wording corrections required before promotion: (i) an atlas must be smooth and surjective, with source an algebraic space or scheme; (ii) W need not be a scheme, so a further scheme presentation is required when Z_(-) is constructed only over schemes, as in CLM-0112-8; (iii) functoriality of the classifying maps is a hypothesis, not a formal consequence of fibre products; (iv) common refinement does not transfer the CE scheme model to atlases of [H/G]. Complementary corroborated findings are compatible rather than duplicates: FND-0180 and FND-0181 already use atlas-independence of this Y on H^bal; FND-0169 shows that compactly supported cohomology of an atlas is not a stack invariant, so the present lemma concerns geometric images only; FND-0187 shows that even after PGL_2-invariance of the classifying map, CLM-0112-8 does not transfer verbatim to etale atlases of Hbar^bal. The candidate kind obstruction is retained as a method-boundary: naive descent of the geometric image, or of the tautological family, across [H/G] fails without a separate invariance (and, for the scheme model, a separate repair).

scope.ground_field: algebraically closed of characteristic zero, or C
hypotheses: H and X are algebraic stacks
atlases are smooth and surjective of finite type, with source an algebraic space (or a scheme)
the classifying morphism is functorial in the 2-Yoneda sense, so tautological families pull back along morphisms of atlases
a morphism [H/G]->X, or equality of geometric images from H and from [H/G], requires a separate G-equivariance/G-invariance hypothesis
not_covered: transfer of the ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 scheme-level P^2-bundle/ordering-torsor model from atlases of H^bal to etale atlases of [H^bal/PGL_2]
atlas-independence of compactly supported cohomology of the atlas
constructibility of S (Chevalley), which is used in CLM-0120-2 but is not required for independence of the reduced closure
Tate type, Gysin maps, closed embeddings of Z, or support-exhaustion
objects: smooth surjective finite-type atlases from algebraic spaces
